YOUR SOLE TASK: audit the ADMIN PORTAL (`app/admin/**`, `components/admin/**`) plus admin-facing lib actions.

Hunt for, in priority order:
P0 — admin controls that can charge/refund/credit a customer wrongly, destroy customer data, or silently corrupt state. Especially: components/admin/RefundControls.tsx, InvoiceAdmin.tsx, components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx, lib/actions-admin-billing.ts, app/admin/grant/page.tsx, lib/actions-gift.ts, app/admin/coupons, lib/actions-nodes.ts (node edits that affect capacity/placement), components/admin/BulkTable.tsx bulk destructive actions.
P1 — dead or lying admin UI: settings toggles persisted but never read by any code; a feature flag written to Settings that no runtime path consumes; status/health badges that are hardcoded or derived from never-updated fields; buttons that call nothing; forms whose action returns success but no-ops; "queued/processing" states that never resolve. CHECK EVERY PANEL under components/admin/settings/** (GeneralPanel, BillingPanel, DomainsPanel, EmailPanel, FeatureFlagsPanel, GrowthPanel, ProvisioningPanel, SecurityPanel, StaffPanel, DedicatedIpPanel) — for each setting key written, grep the repo for a READ of that key. Keys written but never read are the jackpot. Same for lib/settings.ts.
P2 — error paths: admin actions with no error surface, unhandled failures, missing requireAdmin() guards, unvalidated input.
P3 — navigation dead ends: every link/href in the admin sidebar (components/portal/Shell.tsx admin nav) and every admin page — does the target route exist? Any link to a route that 404s? Features referenced in admin nav or docs that don't exist. Also check app/admin/docs, app/admin/improvements, app/admin/email-templates, app/admin/support inbox for broken flows.

Also: verify admin pages correctly refuse to render while impersonating (CLAUDE.md says they should call realUser/requireAdmin).

VERIFY EVERY FINDING by reading code and, where useful, checking the live DB read-only (e.g. does the Settings table actually contain the key?). For each give absolute file:line and a CONCRETE failure scenario ("admin clicks X → Y happens / nothing happens but UI says it worked"). Drop anything you cannot make concrete. Do not pad with style nits.

Return findings directly as your final message (do NOT write any .md file). Order by severity P0→P3, file:line for every item. Also plainly state which admin areas you found SOLID.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

I'm spotting a critical vulnerability in the `refundPayment` method: it processes the Stripe refund before validating the wallet balance, which means a successful Stripe refund could proceed even if the wallet debit fails. More importantly, there's no validation that the refund amount doesn't exceed the original charge or that the transaction hasn't already been refunded.

The method also has a dangerous pattern where it always picks the most recent Stripe top-up transaction regardless of which payment the admin intended to refund — so multiple refund requests could hit the same session, causing Stripe errors that fall back to wallet-only refunds. And there's no idempotency check, so clicking refund twice creates two separate Stripe refunds. The `parseAmountCents` validation catches negative amounts and caps the maximum, which helps, but the core issue remains that the refund logic doesn't track which transactions have already been refunded.

There's also a critical ledger corruption bug: when refunding via Stripe but the wallet balance is insufficient, the code decrements the wallet by only what's available (`walletDebit`), yet records the full refund amount (`-cents`) in the transaction history. This means the ledger no longer sums to the actual balance — if anything recomputes the balance from transaction history, it'll be wrong. The wallet-only path avoids this since `walletDebit` equals `cents`, but I need to check whether any code actually derives balance from summing transactions.

I'm also noticing that `bulkVoidInvoices` voids invoices with status "OPEN" or "REFUNDED", which is odd because voiding a refunded invoice loses the refund record. The doc comment claims it skips paid invoices and ignores already-void ones, but the actual behavior includes refunded ones, and the skipped count includes non-existent IDs. I should present these as connected findings—the primary issue being that coupons don't work in production, with the inversion as a secondary latent defect within that dead system.

I have everything I need. Here are the verified findings.

## P0 — money / destructive / silent corruption

**1. The invoice page's Refund button is not bound to the invoice, and refunds an arbitrary Stripe payment**
`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:56-65` mounts `<RefundControls userId={invoice.user.id} defaultAmount={totalCents} />` under a heading "Refunds & adjustments" on invoice **#N**, pre-filled with that invoice's total. But `refundPayment` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:46-135`) only ever receives `userId` + `amount` — no invoice id. It then picks the refund target with `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:66-70`:
```ts
const tx = await db.walletTransaction.findFirst({
  where: { userId, description: { contains: "Stripe payment (cs_" } },
  orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
});
```
Failure: admin opens invoice #12 ($24, from March), clicks the pre-filled **Refund** → Stripe refunds $24 against the customer's *most recent* card top-up (say July's $200), which has nothing to do with invoice #12. Invoice #12's status is never touched (stays OPEN/PAID), no refund link is recorded, and there is no idempotency key — clicking **Refund** twice creates **two** Stripe refunds and two ledger debits. The button is not disabled after success (`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/RefundControls.tsx:50-52` only disables while `pending`).

**2. Refund writes a ledger row that doesn't match the balance change**
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:90-115`: `walletDebit = Math.min(cents, available)`, but the ledger row is always `amountCents: -cents`:
```ts
if (walletDebit > 0) { ...balanceCents: { decrement: walletDebit } }
await tx.walletTransaction.create({ data: { userId, amountCents: -cents, description } });
```
Failure: customer has $5 wallet, admin refunds $50 to their card. Stripe leg succeeds → balance drops $5, ledger records **−$50**. The customer's transaction history and their balance permanently disagree by $45 with no explanation. The doc comment at line 44 promises "the rest is a real-cash write-off **and note it**" — the description built at lines 99-103 contains no such note.

**3. The "Auto-suspend overdue accounts" toggle is dead — it cannot stop suspensions**
`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx:43-48` ships a toggle hinted "Let the billing sweep suspend servers once the terminate threshold is reached." It is written by `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-settings.ts:51`. **Zero reads exist anywhere in the repo** (verified by whole-repo grep — only settings.ts/actions-settings.ts/BillingPanel.tsx mention `auto_suspend_enabled`). The sweep at `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:192-215` suspends unconditionally.
Failure: an incident forces the admin to pause suspensions; they turn the toggle **off** and see "Saved." The next sweep (≤10 min) still queues `SUSPEND` jobs and knocks customer VMs offline. Same for the three dunning-day fields (`dunning_grace_days` / `warn` / `terminate`, `BillingPanel.tsx:24-26`) — never read; `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:27,31,33` uses `process.env.NXEON_GRACE_DAYS ?? 3` / `NXEON_TERMINATE_DAYS ?? 10` / `NXEON_WARN_BEFORE_TERMINATE_DAYS ?? 2`, and none of those env vars are set in `.env`, so the values are hardcoded 3/10/2 regardless of what the panel shows.

**4. Node `natChain` / `subnetPrefix` are validated and stored but the worker ignores them**
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts:21` documents `natChain` as "the iptables chain the worker rebuilds from the DB"; `:128-131` enforces global uniqueness; `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx:24-25` pre-fills `NXEON_FWD_N2` / `10.20.1.`. But `/opt/nxeon/worker/network.ts:7` hardcodes `const CHAIN = process.env.NXEON_NAT_CHAIN ?? "NXEON_FWD"`, and `syncPortForwards()` (`:32-54`) selects **every** server regardless of node and DNATs them all into that one chain. `Node.natChain` has no consumer anywhere (`lib/ipam.ts:89` returns it into a range object that nothing reads).
Failure: admin registers node-2 via `/admin/nodes/new` and provisions a VM there (guest `10.20.1.101`). The worker flushes `NXEON_FWD` **on the primary host** and adds a DNAT to `10.20.1.101:22` — an address that host cannot route. `NXEON_FWD_N2` is never created on node-2. Every node-2 VM has dead SSH while `/admin/nodes` shows the node green/ONLINE.
Compounding: `updateNode` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts:174-200`) lets an admin change `subnetPrefix`, `ipStart/ipEnd`, `natChain` and `bridge` on a node that already has servers — there is no `_count.servers` guard (only `deleteNode:292` has one). Editing the subnet on the live primary node makes `lib/ipam.ts:168` (`where: { ipAddress: { startsWith: range.subnetPrefix } }`) stop seeing the existing leases, so the next provision hands out an IP already in use.

## P1 — dead / lying admin UI

**5. The Settings → Email template editor is completely inert**
`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/EmailPanel.tsx:19` mounts `<EmailTemplateEditor />`, backed by `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-templates.ts` (save/toggle/reset against `db.emailTemplate`, 20 seeded rows all `enabled: true` — confirmed in the live DB). The only code path that reads those rows is `renderTemplate()` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/email-render.ts:220-249`, reachable only via `sendMail({ template })` / `sendTemplate()` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/mailer.ts:118-128, 166-175`). **Those have zero call sites.** Every real send passes explicit `subject` + `html` from the code catalog:
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions.ts:135-136` (welcome), `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-account.ts:129-130, 171-172` (password reset), `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe.ts:254-255` (receipt), `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-newsletter-campaign.ts:204`.

Failure: admin rewrites the "Welcome" subject/body in Settings → Email, sees **"Saved."** (`EmailTemplateEditor.tsx:160`), and every new customer still receives the untouched hardcoded template from `lib/email-templates.ts`. The enable/disable checkbox (`:237`) is equally inert. Note the sibling page `/admin/email-templates` is honest — it's read-only and badged "code-managed" (`app/admin/email-templates/page.tsx:192`); the *editable* copy inside Settings is the lie.

**6. The entire Coupons admin area is inert in this production config**
`.env` has `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live…`, so `stripeConfigured()` is true. `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:113` then **hides** the only redemption surface: `{!stripeConfigured() && (<CouponField />)}`. And the Stripe credit path (`/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe.ts:215-245`) never reads the coupon cookie, never applies `bonusCents`, never writes a `CouponRedemption`. The customer page even comments this honestly at `:108-112`.
Failure: admin creates `LAUNCH20` on `/admin/coupons`, the table shows it green **active** with `0 / 100` redeemed forever. No customer can enter it anywhere. The Growth panel's "Coupons enabled" toggle (`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/GrowthPanel.tsx:20-25`, hint "Turn off to hide the promo-code field platform-wide") governs a field that is already unconditionally hidden.
Latent inside this: the **`FIXED_CENTS` coupon kind is inverted**. The admin dropdown labels it "Fixed cents off" (`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/CouponControls.tsx:34`) and `/admin/coupons` renders it "$5.00 off" (`/opt/nxeon/lib/growth.ts:56-57`), but `couponBonusForTopup` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-growth.ts:44-54`) returns it as a bonus, and `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions.ts:543` does `increment: cents + bonusCents`. A "$5 off" coupon **gives** the customer $5 rather than discounting. Also `ANY`/`ORDER` scope options (`CouponControls.tsx:45-49`) have no order-side implementation at all — `applyCouponToTopup` hard-rejects `ORDER` (`actions-growth.ts:80-82`) and `lib/order.ts` never touches coupons.

**7. `referral_reward_cents` is never read**
`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/GrowthPanel.tsx:12-19` ("Credited to both referrer and referred user"). The actual payout is `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-growth.ts:263` → `referralRewardCents()` → `/opt/nxeon/lib/growth.ts:13-16`, which reads only `process.env.REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS` (not set in `.env`) → hardcoded 500. `/opt/nxeon/lib/affiliate.ts:42` only *mentions* the key in a comment.
Failure: admin raises the referral reward to $10 for a campaign, sees "Saved.", every referral still pays $5. (By contrast `signup_free_credit_cents` **is** correctly wired at `actions-growth.ts:234`.)

**8. `domain_markup_percent` is never read — and the panel displays the wrong number**
`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/DomainsPanel.tsx:12-20`. Real pricing is `/opt/nxeon/lib/registrar.ts:62-71`: `Number(process.env.DOMAIN_MARKUP_PCT ?? 25)`, applied by `retailCents()` at `:92, 94, 258, 308`. `DOMAIN_MARKUP_PCT` is not set in `.env`.
Failure: the live `Setting` table has **no** `domain_markup_percent` row (verified — only 7 rows exist), so `getAllSettings()` falls back to the default `"0"` and the Domains panel tells the admin **markup is 0%** while customers are actually being charged **25%** over registrar cost. Changing it to 40 and saving changes nothing. `whois_privacy_default` (`DomainsPanel.tsx:21-26`, "Pre-selects free WHOIS privacy in the domain checkout") likewise has zero reads — no checkout code consults it.

**9. Ten more setting keys written with no reader**
Verified zero reads outside `lib/settings.ts` / `lib/actions-settings.ts` / the panel that writes them:
- `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:12-21` — `brand_name`, `brand_tagline`, `support_email`, `company_legal_name`, `company_address`, `social_twitter/github/discord/linkedin`, `footer_text`. `company_address`'s own placeholder says "shown on invoices"; `/opt/nxeon/lib/invoices.ts` never reads it. Renaming the platform in "Platform name" changes nothing anywhere.

(For contrast, these *are* correctly wired: `livechat_snippet`, `currency`, `tax_percent`, `min_topup_cents`, `volume_price_cents_per_gb`, `extra_disk_gb_price_cents`, all three `dedicated_ip_*`, `max_servers_per_user`, `signup_free_credit_cents`, `maintenance_mode/_message`, `coupons_enabled`, all six `smtp_*`, `enforce_staff_2fa`, `session_length_days`, `login_ratelimit_max`, `allowed_admin_ips`, and all five `feature_*` flags.)

**10. `/admin/automation` status badges are hardcoded green**
`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/automation/page.tsx:52, 82, 109, 132` — four `<StatusDot status="online" …>` literals for "Provisioning worker", "Billing sweep", "Port-forward sync" and "Improvement agent". setMsg(`${action.label}: ${ids.length} row${…} done.`);

## P2 — error paths

**15. `InvoiceAdminActions` treats a redirect as a failure surface, and `GenerateInvoiceButton` has no confirm.** `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/InvoiceAdmin.tsx:17-27` catches and displays `e.message`; `markInvoicePaid`/`voidInvoice` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-billing.ts:55, 71`) call `requireAdmin()` which `redirect()`s — a BILLING-role staffer (who can reach `/admin/invoices/[id]`, gated only on `requireArea("billing")` at `app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:23`) clicking **Mark paid** gets an opaque `NEXT_REDIRECT` string in the red error span instead of a permission message. **16. Coupon toggle/delete have no error surface.** `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/CouponControls.tsx:85` and `:100` call `adminToggleCoupon` / `adminDeleteCoupon` (both `Promise<void>`, `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-growth.ts:197, 212`) inside `startTransition` with no `try/catch` and no `router.refresh()`. ## P3 — navigation

**Clean.** I resolved all 41 hrefs in `/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-groups.ts` against `app/admin/**/page.tsx` — every one has a real page, zero 404s. `/admin/nodes/new` is the only page not in the nav and it is correctly linked from `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/page.tsx:37, 47`. `/admin/improvements` and `/admin/docs` are absent from `HREF_AREA` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:44-84`) but that falls through to `"platform"` (ADMIN-only) at `:87`, which matches their page guards.

## Areas I found SOLID

- **Impersonation refusal** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/layout.tsx:63-67` uses `realUser()` then redirects to `/dashboard` if `impersonating()`, and `requireArea` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:99-105`) independently resolves via `realUser()`. Matches CLAUDE.md.
- **Guard coverage** — all 47 admin pages call `requireArea(...)`; I checked every one. Plus the host gate (`layout.tsx:10-16`), IP allow-list with a deliberate fail-open (`:37-57`), and staff-2FA enforcement (`:95-97`).
- **`lib/actions-settings.ts`** — the section→field map is server-side so the key list is never client-supplied; the `secret` branch (`:130-135`) correctly refuses to clobber a stored secret with blank, and `app/admin/settings/page.tsx:49-52` strips `SECRET_KEYS` before handing values to the browser. The *plumbing* is right; only the downstream consumers are missing.
- **`lib/actions-nodes.ts`** validation — subnet/port/chain collision checks, single-primary enforcement, and `deleteNode`'s refusal on primary + attached servers (`:291-296`) are all correct.
- **`lib/actions-gift.ts`** — race-safe redemption via `updateMany` guarded on `redeemedById: null` inside a transaction (`:117-137`), and `adminDeleteGiftCode` refuses redeemed codes (`:91`).
- **`worker/billing.ts` renewal** — CAS on `expiresAt` plus atomic `debitWallet` (`:129-136`) genuinely prevents double-charging; the dedicated-IP surcharge correctly bills off the `DedicatedIp` row rather than the intent flag (`:113-115`).
- **`lib/actions-improvements.ts`** — `bulkSetStatus` refuses a fully unconstrained update (`:79-80`), and status strings are asserted before use.
- **`/admin/docs`** and **`/admin/email-templates`** (the read-only one) are honest: docs reads real markdown off disk with server-side sanitization, and the template preview is explicitly badged "code-managed".
